questions.enonce_markdown:
The parametric equations of a curve are given by $x = 1 + t$, $y = 2 + \dfrac1t$, $t \neq 0$ is a parameter.

Show that an equation of the normal to the curve at the point where $t = 2$ is $8x - 2y - 19 = 0$.

Find the value of $t$ at the point where this normal meets the curve again. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Gradient of the curve.** $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 1$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{t^2}$, so
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = -\frac{1}{t^2}.$$

**At $t = 2$:** the point is $\left(1 + 2,\; 2 + \tfrac12\right) = \left(3, \tfrac52\right)$ and the gradient of the tangent is $-\tfrac14$. The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its gradient is $-1 \big/ \left(-\tfrac14\right) = 4$. The normal is
$$y - \tfrac52 = 4(x - 3) \;\Longrightarrow\; 2y - 5 = 8x - 24 \;\Longrightarrow\; 8x - 2y - 19 = 0. \qquad \blacksquare$$

**Where the normal meets the curve again.** Substitute $x = 1 + t$ and $y = 2 + \tfrac1t$ into the equation of the normal:
$$8(1 + t) - 2\left(2 + \frac1t\right) - 19 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; 8t - 15 - \frac2t = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; 8t^2 - 15t - 2 = 0.$$
This quadratic in $t$ has the known root $t = 2$ (the given point), so it factorises as
$$(t - 2)(8t + 1) = 0.$$
The other root is $t = -\tfrac18$.

$$\boxed{t = -\tfrac18}$$

**Check:** at $t = -\tfrac18$ the point is $x = \tfrac78$, $y = 2 - 8 = -6$; then $8\left(\tfrac78\right) - 2(-6) - 19 = 7 + 12 - 19 = 0$, so it lies on the normal.

questions.enonce_markdown: A new primary school intends to recruit a head teacher and 7 other teachers. There are 3 male and 2 female applicants for the position of head teacher, 4 male and 6 female other applicants for the teaching positions. Find the number of different ways of selecting the staff of 8 if gender equity must be respected. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Interpretation.** The statement does not define "gender equity". It is taken to mean equal numbers of men and women on the staff of 8, that is **4 male and 4 female** staff members in total (head teacher included). The head teacher is chosen from the 5 head-teacher applicants (3 male, 2 female) and the 7 other teachers from the 10 other applicants (4 male, 6 female).

**Case 1: the head teacher is male** (3 ways). The other 7 teachers must then be $4 - 1 = 3$ male and 4 female:
$$3 \times \binom43\binom64 = 3 \times 4 \times 15 = 180.$$

**Case 2: the head teacher is female** (2 ways). The other 7 teachers must be 4 male and $4 - 1 = 3$ female:
$$2 \times \binom44\binom63 = 2 \times 1 \times 20 = 40.$$

The cases are mutually exclusive, so add them:
$$180 + 40 = \boxed{220 \text{ different ways}}$$

(The 7 other teachers are a selection, not an arrangement, so combinations are used; the head teacher is a distinct post, which is why it is chosen separately.)
